title: Training Periodization, Methods, Intensity Distribution, and Volume in Highly Trained and Elite Distance Runners: A Systematic Review
authors: Casado A, Gonzalez-Mohino F, Gonzalez-Rave JM, Foster C
journal: International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance
population: Highly trained and elite middle- and long-distance runners; 10 articles
findings: Highly trained/elite distance runners typically follow a pyramidal TID, with volume decreasing from zone 1 (at or below vLT1) to zone 2 (between vLT1 and vLT2) to zone 3 (above vLT2).

Continuous tempo or interval work at vLT2 (zone 2) and zone 3 sessions were each used at least once a week by elite runners, and the number of vLT2 or zone 3 sessions was increased to tilt toward a pyramidal or a polarized approach respectively.
Marathoners used more pyramidal and 1500 m runners more polarized approaches.
Authors encourage a hard-day/easy-day pattern and a shift from pyramidal in preparatory and pre-competitive periods to polarized in the competitive period.
Highly trained and elite distance runners typically follow a pyramidal intensity distribution: decreasing volume from zone 1 (at or below first ventilatory/lactate threshold) to zone 2 to zone 3.

Continuous-tempo or interval sessions at vLT2 (zone 2) and zone 3 sessions were each used at least once per week in elite runners, to adopt a more pyramidal or polarized approach respectively; marathoners used more pyramidal and 1500 m runners more polarized approaches.

Conclusion: runners are encouraged to adopt a traditional periodization pattern on a hard day-easy day basis, shifting from pyramidal TID in the preparatory and pre-competitive periods toward polarized TID in the competitive period.
limitations: Ten articles, mostly observational, heterogeneous zone definitions, elite and male-dominated. The periodization recommendation is the authors' synthesis and has not been tested by RCT. Level lowered from A to B because it synthesises descriptive data.
implications: Default distance-runner template is pyramidal (zone 1 > zone 2 > zone 3) with about one threshold-zone session and one zone 3 session per week in build phases (elite practice; scale down for lower-volume runners).
Tilt by event: marathon and longer more pyramidal; shorter events may move toward polarized in the competitive phase.
Hard/easy alternation is an elite-runner recommendation; extending it to recreational runners is a conservative inference.

Default structure: traditional periodization with hard day-easy day (quality sessions separated by at least one easy or rest day); 1-2 quality sessions per week for recreational runners is an extrapolation (grade D).
Pyramidal intensity distribution in base/build; allow a polarized shift in the final specific phase for 5-10 km goals; keep marathon and longer pyramidal (extrapolated beyond marathon).

verification.notes: Crossref matches IJSPP 2022-06-01. Claims confirmed in abstract. Researcher's 'no consecutive hard days for recreational athletes' reworded as inference.
